#+TITLE: Overlapping CLOCK lines

Every CLOCK line here is individually canonical (``clock check``
passes) but several pairs cover the same instant, so
``clock overlap`` must report them and exit 1.

* Partial overlap
:PROPERTIES:
:TASK_REF: 10
:END:
:LOGBOOK:
CLOCK: [2026-02-02 Mon 10:00 +0100]--[2026-02-02 Mon 12:00 +0100] =>  2:00
CLOCK: [2026-02-02 Mon 11:00 +0100]--[2026-02-02 Mon 13:00 +0100] =>  2:00
:END:

One hour shared: 11:00 to 12:00.

* Full containment
:PROPERTIES:
:TASK_REF: 11
:END:
:LOGBOOK:
CLOCK: [2026-02-03 Tue 09:00 +0100]--[2026-02-03 Tue 18:00 +0100] =>  9:00
CLOCK: [2026-02-03 Tue 12:00 +0100]--[2026-02-03 Tue 13:00 +0100] =>  1:00
:END:

The inner hour is entirely inside the outer day.

* Exact duplicate
:PROPERTIES:
:TASK_REF: 12
:END:
:LOGBOOK:
CLOCK: [2026-02-04 Wed 14:00 +0100]--[2026-02-04 Wed 15:00 +0100] =>  1:00
CLOCK: [2026-02-04 Wed 14:00 +0100]--[2026-02-04 Wed 15:00 +0100] =>  1:00
:END:

The same hour logged twice.

* Overlap across a timezone change
:PROPERTIES:
:TASK_REF: 13
:END:
:LOGBOOK:
CLOCK: [2026-02-05 Thu 08:00 +0100]--[2026-02-05 Thu 10:00 +0100] =>  2:00
CLOCK: [2026-02-05 Thu 15:30 +0800]--[2026-02-05 Thu 17:00 +0800] =>  1:30
:END:

07:00Z-09:00Z against 07:30Z-09:00Z: the local times look
unrelated, but the instants collide for ninety minutes.
